newsitem.title: USA: Sony Corp. names former CBS executive head of U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Sony Corp. names former CBS executive head of U.S. unit.

text.p: Howard Stringer, the former president of CBS's broadcast group and CBS News, on Thursday was named president of Sony Corp. of America.
He is to assume his new position on May 5.

Stringer is to work closely with Sony's operating companies, including Sony Electronics Inc., Sony Music Entertainment Inc. and its Sony Pictures Entertainment Hollywood studio, to coordinate group-wide efforts to expand Sony's business.

Most recently, Stringer was chairman and chief executive of TELE-TV, a partnership formed by three telecommunications companies in 1994. He was named chairman and chief executive of TELE-TV in March 1995.

Earlier this month, the partnership made up of Bell Atlantic Corp., NYNEX Corp. and Pacific Telesis Group said they were scaling back TELE-TV and eliminating 100 jobs, about half of its total work force.

TELE-TV had been formed to develop home entertainment, information and interactive services. Stringer spent 30 years at CBS television, where he served as president of CBS Broadcast Group and president of CBS News, leaving in 1995 to join TELE-TV.
